neighbours.label: A verb of occurring, after a relative or 'whatever': 'that took place', 'that has emerged', 'whatever happens at', 'that broke out'; the same clause with an agent doing something stays quiet
fire: The meeting that took place last week was short.
One problem that has arisen is the cost of fuel.
A fight that broke out at the bar ended in arrests.
Another trend that has emerged is working from home.
Events that occurred before the war are hard to date.
Whatever happens at the trial, he will lose his job.
The changes that take place during puberty are large.
The crisis that developed in spring lasted a year.
quiet: The meeting that I chaired last week was short.
One problem that we solved is the cost of fuel.
A man that fought at the bar paid for the arrests.
Another trend that I like is working from home.
Events that historians studied before the war are hard to date.
Whatever he says at the trial, he will lose his job.
The changes that parents notice during puberty are large.
The crisis that she described in spring lasted a year.

short: verb of occurring (took place, emerged, broke out)
notes: Card: ' place' x6 after take, ' at' x3 after develops or transpires, ' emerged' x3, ' arise' x3, ' depends'. Probe: 'that takes place' 1.06, 'took place' 0.92, 'what develops at' 0.92, 'that has emerged' 0.89, 'Whatever transpires at' 0.60; 'that takes coffee' 0.06, 'has been discussed' 0.24, sentence-initial 'Problems arise' 0.02. So the relative or whatever clause may matter as much as the verb.
